votes.evidence: I read both videos sequentially (535 frames each) because cv2 seeking gave a misaligned raw frame, then compared annotated frame 140 (HUD reads "frame 140 shot 1") with the raw frame. The HUD says "A (white gi): LOST (no pose)". The only red pixels in the whole frame are the HUD text, at x 12-277 and y 10-27, so no A box, skeleton or label is drawn. A zoom shows the white-gi athlete in plain view mid-throw, with torso, hips, both legs, a foot at about (528,480) and head at about (555,310). The white athlete extends below and to the right of the blue athlete. Only B is drawn: a green dashed colour-split box (x 302-552, y 185-447) with a green skeleton, which partly overlaps the white athlete but is labelled B. Annotated frame: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Grappling-rig-app-v2/9af305d0-b71a-552d-b344-ad580d75284a/scratchpad/verify/fs_ann_140.png. Raw frame: .../verify/fs_raw_140.png (an earlier set-seek raw_140.png shows a different moment and should be ignored). Zoom: .../verify/fs_zoom_140.png. The error is present: A is dropped while clearly visible.

The claim holds at exactly frame 140. The annotated frame (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Grappling-rig-app-v2/9af305d0-b71a-552d-b344-ad580d75284a/scratchpad/verify/ann_140.png) has HUD "A (white gi): LOST (no pose)". It draws only a green B box, a dashed colour-split box with 0.40 on the blue athlete, and no red box, skeleton or label. A cv2 seek (set(1,F)) returned a different scene, so I re-read both videos sequentially. That raw frame matches the annotated one (mean pixel difference about 2.5 in the central region), so I used it (rawseq_140.png). It shows the white-gi athlete clearly in plain view, mid-throw. Her white legs and lower torso sit at the lower right of the blue athlete, from about x 410-550 and y 270-490. Her head is visible at about (560,310), and one foot is planted on the mat near (530,470). Nothing hides her; she is only partly overlapped by blue's arm and body. The temporal check shows a one-frame dropout. At frame 137 A is "colour-split" with a red dashed box over the white-gi area. At frame 143 A is "colour-split 0.25" with a red dashed box near her torso. Frame 140 sits between them with no A overlay at all. The tangled-frame allowance covers partial boxes or missing pose fragments, but here there is no box of any kind for a large visible white-gi region, so this is lost_but_visible. Severity high is reasonable because A disappears completely for the frame, though it recovers by 143.

votes.evidence: I extracted frame 308 from /home/user/Grappling-rig-app_v2/outputs/annotated.mp4 and zoomed in. The HUD reads "A (white gi): LOST (no pose)" and there is no red box, skeleton or label anywhere. Only B has an overlay, a green dashed colour-split box labelled "B (blue gi) colour-split 0.40" on the blue athlete at about x 375-490, y 320-435. The white-gi athlete is plainly visible in the same frame. He lies prone on the mat with white-gi legs and lower body running right to about x 770, bare feet at the far right, and white gi under the blue athlete on the left. The referee's black leg crosses the middle of the white-gi athlete's body, but it hides only a narrow slice. Most of his torso and legs are still seen, so A is lost while visible, as the auditor said. The raw clip seek for frame 308 returned a slightly different moment (clock 2:07, not 2:08), so I judged from the annotated frame, which shows the scene clearly. The claim holds.

In annotated frame 308 (/home/user/Grappling-rig-app_v2/outputs/annotated.mp4), the HUD reads "A (white gi): LOST (no pose)" and no red box, label or skeleton is drawn. Only B (blue gi, colour-split 0.40) has a dashed green box. The white-gi athlete is plainly visible on the mat to the right of the blue athlete, at roughly x 530-770 and y 410-470. Their white legs, bare feet and hip area are clear, and the referee's leg crosses only part of the torso. So the claim is accurate at this frame, although "unobstructed" slightly understates the referee's leg occlusion. This is a one-frame dropout, not a consistent wrong-athlete overlay. Frame 305 has an A box (colour-split 0.16, small and poor). Frames 306 and 307 have colour-recovered A boxes. Frames 309 (colour-recovered) and 310 (detected 0.19) have A boxes on the white athlete, and frame 311 has one covering the white legs. The claim concerns frame 308 itself, and A is dropped there while clearly visible. This is a genuine lost_but_visible error. The "high" severity is debatable because the dropout lasts one frame, but the error is present. The raw clip frame 308 did not align temporally with the annotated frame 308 in my pixel comparison, so I judged from the annotated frame and its neighbours.

The HUD reads "A (white gi): LOST (no pose)" and there is no red box, skeleton or label anywhere in the frame. Only B has overlays: a green dashed box labelled "B (blue gi) colour-split 0.40" and a green skeleton on the blue athlete's back.

The white-gi athlete is plainly visible mid-throw, so A is lost but visible. I checked this on the annotated frame and on the matching raw frame (k_raw124.png, zoomed in k_zoom_raw.png). The athlete has dark hair and a white gi and is tipped over, with legs and feet in the air. The head is at roughly x=560-600, y=310-370. The white torso runs down-right through about (500-560, 380-440), and the legs and feet reach about (540-580, 440-490). The blue athlete is upright but bent over at left, with motion blur.

This is a total miss, not a partial box. B's dashed box sits on the blue athlete and clips only part of the white torso. Nothing at all is drawn on the white athlete's head, legs or feet.

One wording caveat in the claim: the white athlete is entangled with the blue athlete and extends right and below, rather than sitting cleanly to the right. This does not change the verdict.

The raw clip does not line up with the annotated video at the same frame index. Annotated 142 matches raw frame about 124 by image difference, and the scoreboard shows 2:13 versus 2:12 at raw 142. This does not affect the verdict, because the annotated frame shows the problem by itself.

At frame 142 the claim holds. The annotated frame (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Grappling-rig-app-v2/9af305d0-b71a-552d-b344-ad580d75284a/scratchpad/verify/ann_142.png) has the HUD line "A (white gi): LOST (no pose)". It shows no red box, skeleton or label anywhere. Only B has a dashed green colour-split box, a label (0.40) and a skeleton on the blue athlete. The raw picture at frame 142 (rawseq_142.png, read sequentially) shows the white-gi athlete clearly mid-throw. He is just right of the blue athlete, with dark hair, his head at about x=570,y=330, white gi, and feet in the air near x=545,y=470. A is plainly visible, so this is lost_but_visible.

Seeking: my first raw extraction used cv2 seek and landed on the wrong moment (blue standing, white on the mat). I redid it by sequential read. The mean absolute difference between the annotated and raw frames is 4.4 at index 142 and 14 or more at the neighbouring indices, so the sequential frames are aligned. The claim is judged on the aligned frame.

Temporal context: this is a flicker, not a persistent wrong-athlete overlay. Frame 139 has A as colour-split (no pose) with a dashed red box on the white athlete. Frame 140 is also LOST. Frames 141, 143 and 144 are colour-split with no pose. Frame 145 has a detected solid red box on the white athlete, with skeleton and a 0.20 score. So the tracker drops A to LOST at 140 and 142, and frame 142 itself has no A overlay although A is clearly visible. The error is momentary but really present at the exact frame.
